messages.subject: Second-order CFA - Measurement Invariance
parts:
Hi everyone! How can I test for measurement invariance of thresholds (I am employing WLSMV to deal with categorical manfiest items) and factor loadings in a second-order CFA?



First, I estimate a simultaneous first-order CFA with WLSMV.  I apply the model on the object that results from multiple imputation. --> I test for measurement invariance across categories of gender (male and female), constraining both thresholds and factor loadings. The output seems fine, and fit indices are ok (RMSEA < 0.05, TLI>0.95, CFI>0.95).

 

cfa_1 =        "life_satisfaction =~ stflife + stflfsf + stfsdlv

                      pos_affect =~        wrhpp + enjlf + enrglot + fltpcfl

                      neg_affect =~        fltanx + fltsd + fltdpr + cldgng + flteeff + flttrd + fltbrd"

 

colnames= c("stflife","stflfsf","stfsdlv", "wrhpp","enjlf","enrglot","fltpcfl","fltanx","fltsd","fltdpr","cldgng","flteeff","flttrd","fltbrd")

complete.cfa_1 = runMI(

  model = cfa_1,          

  data = amelia.output$imputations,

  fun="cfa",

  estimator = "WLSMV",

  ordered=colnames,

  group="gndr",

  group.equal=c("thresholds","loadings))

 

Second, I estimate a second-order CFA. with WLSMV.  I apply the model on the object that results from multiple imputation. --> I want to test for measurement invariance, constraining both thresholds and factor loadings, BUT IT DOESN'T WORK.... I get the message "higher-order factors detected. ID.fac set to "ul", followed by the warning  "the model did not converge for any imputed datasets". 


Have I made any mistake in the measEq.syntax function?  I don't understand why this doesn't work due to the following 2 reasons: 

  • When I focus on the second-order CFA and use group.equal=c("loadings"), rather than group.equal=c("loadings","regressions","thresholds"), it works fine.
  • Also, when I focus on the simultaneous first-order CFA model (described above) and constrain the thresholds to be equal, the model's fit is quite ok. 

 

cfa_1 =       "life_satisfaction =~ stflife + stflfsf + stfsdlv

                      pos_affect =~        wrhpp + enjlf + enrglot + fltpcfl

                      neg_affect =~        fltanx + fltsd + fltdpr + cldgng + flteeff + flttrd + fltbrd

                      wellbeing =~         life_satisfaction + pos_affect + neg_affect

                      "

colnames= c("stflife","stflfsf","stfsdlv", "wrhpp","enjlf","enrglot","fltpcfl","fltanx","fltsd","fltdpr","cldgng","flteeff","flttrd","fltbrd")

config.cfa_1 = runMI(

  model = cfa_1,          

  data = amelia.output$imputations,

  fun="cfa",

  estimator = "WLSMV",

  ordered=colnames,

  group="gndr",

  std.lv = TRUE

)

 

config.cfa_2 = measEq.syntax(configural.model=config.cfa_1,

                       group="gndr",

                       group.equal=c("loadings","regressions","thresholds"),

                       ID.fac = "std.lv",

                       ID.cat = "default",

                       return.fit=TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: Second-order CFA - Measurement Invariance
parts: It might help to post your full script in sequence, not pieces of it interrupted by narrative.  Your examples above have 2 different "cfa_1" models.
How can I test for measurement invariance of thresholds
How many categories are there?
I apply the model on the object that results from multiple imputation.
Try first checking your syntax on a single imputation using lavaan(), to resolve all your issues before applying the syntax to multiple imputations with lavaan.mi()
I get the message "higher-order factors detected. ID.fac set to "ul",
That is explain in the help-page details.  Just set the argument yourself if you don't want to see the message.
Have I made any mistake in the measEq.syntax function?

For CFAs with higher-order factors, you need to identify the factors by fixing the first loading (ID.fac = "ul" or "auto.fix.first").  I recommend fitting the configural model with that constraint, because the measEq.syntax() function is designed to respect any fixed (to 0 or other values) parameters in your configural model.

I am checking whether there is invariance measurement across the two categories of gender (male and female). The model is the cfa_1 syntax below. All of the 14 manifest indicators (in colnames vector below) are ordinal variables with 4 response categories. Thus,  the WLSMV estimator estimates 3*14=52 thresholds. 

As you suggested, I apply the model first on the original dataset (without multiple imputation). I also include the auto.fix.first=TRUE argument in the function for the configural model. 

Yet, I now receive the warning: "The configural.model argument is a lavaan model fitted using auto-fix-first=TRUE (or std.lv=FALSE), which conflicts with the requested "ID.fac" method. To generate syntax using the fixed-factor or effects-coding method of identification, set std.lv=TRUE to prevent initial loadings from being fixed to 1 in the syntax". 

How can I solve this?

The code is below:

cfa_1 =       "life_satisfaction =~ stflife + stflfsf + stfsdlv

                      pos_affect =~        wrhpp + enjlf + enrglot + fltpcfl

                      neg_affect =~        fltanx + fltsd + fltdpr + cldgng + flteeff + flttrd + fltbrd

                      wellbeing =~         life_satisfaction + pos_affect + neg_affect"

config.cfa_1 = cfa(

  model = cfa_1,          

  data = dataframe,

estimator = "WLSMV",

  ordered=colnames,

  group="gndr",
auto.fix.first=TRUE

)

 

config.cfa_2 = measEq.syntax(configural.model=config.cfa_1,

                       group="gndr",

group.equal=c("loadings","thresholds"),
